headline: EU issues binding DMA specifications for Google AI interoperability and search-data access
summary: On July 16, 2026, the European Commission issued two binding specification measures to Google under the Digital Markets Act. One addresses Android interoperability so users can invoke competing AI assistants and delegate actions in apps; the other specifies access for eligible third-party search engines, including AI chatbots with search functions, to anonymized Google Search ranking, query, click and view data. The rules define eligibility, data scope, use limits, privacy safeguards, audits, access processes and FRAND pricing. Google's own program page says the specified dataset covers the European Economic Area and that qualifying recipients must accept licensing terms. This review did not establish that applicants have received data or that the measures have changed competition or user outcomes.
